title: Adic scalar data and normalized flat reduction complexes
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\pi$, and put $A_n=R/\pi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $T$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme]. On its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] write $\underline M_T$ for the constant sheaf of an $R$-module $M$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and put $B_T=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_T$, with projections $\operatorname{pr}_{T,n}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $P^\bullet$ be a specified bounded complex of finite projective $R$-modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], and put $M_T^\bullet=B_T\otimes_{\underline R_T}\underline{P^\bullet}_T$ and $D_{T,n}^\bullet=(A_n)_T\otimes_{\underline R_T}\underline{P^\bullet}_T$, with the given scalar differentials [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Use sheaves of modules and their ambient unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

The ring $R$ is Noetherian, and $(R,(\pi))$ satisfies the adic coefficient datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]: every $A_n$ is finite, is killed by a power of $\ell$, and has the finite free resolution $[R\xrightarrow{\pi^n}R]$ in degrees $-1,0$. The coefficient sheaves of this datum are the displayed constant finite sheaves, and their completed limit and all quotient projections agree with $B_T$ and $\operatorname{pr}_{T,n}$.

For every $r$, $\underline{P^r}_T$ is flat over $\underline R_T$, and $M_T^\bullet$ is a bounded K-flat complex with flat terms over $B_T$ [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, def-pc-kflat-complex]. There are finite-free splitting maps $i_r:P^r\to R^{m_r}$, $s_r:R^{m_r}\to P^r$ with $s_ri_r=1$; their constant realizations and scalar extensions to $B_T$ and every $(A_n)_T$ retain this identity and commute with quotient transitions. Splittings are only asserted degreewise, not as splittings of complexes.

The K-flat computation counit for derived reduction [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] followed by balanced tensor cancellation gives a natural isomorphism in $D((A_n)_T)$
$$M_T^\bullet\otimes^L_{B_T}(A_n)_T\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{T,n}^\bullet.$$
Its ordinary chain representative sends $(b\otimes p)\otimes a$ to $a\operatorname{pr}_{T,n}(b)\otimes p$, with inverse $a\otimes p\mapsto(1\otimes p)\otimes a$. It intertwines every original differential, every consecutive quotient transition, and the canonical reduction unit $b\otimes p\mapsto(b\otimes p)\otimes1$ with the quotient augmentation $b\otimes p\mapsto\operatorname{pr}_{T,n}(b)\otimes p$. These comparisons are natural in chain maps of bounded finite-projective scalar complexes and do not depend on the chosen splittings. Site object, morphism and coefficient universes can be independently enlarged under the smallness convention [def-weil-size-convention].

proof.text: Use the proved adic-ring domain theorem to obtain the datum with ideal (pi), finiteness and l-power annihilation of every quotient. The nonzero uniformizer gives injectivity of multiplication by its powers. Quotient equality to zero and singleton-ideal membership identify the kernel with that image; the quotient map is surjective.

source.place: DVR quotient arithmetic; elementary singleton-ideal kernel calculation.

proof.text: Construct the sheaf of continuous functions with values in the discrete coefficient ring, allowing independent site and coefficient universes. Mathlib proves its sheaf condition by restriction of the fpqc continuous-map sheaf. The map from constant functions is locally injective (use the empty cover on an empty scheme) and locally surjective on the open fibres of a locally constant function. The locally bijective sheafification criterion gives its isomorphism with the constant ring sheaf. Factor continuous functions uniquely through connected components; evaluate sheafification naturality to prove constants, restrictions and quotient postcomposition. Evaluation preserves the inverse limit, so its universal property gives the unique compatible completed section.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.12; continuous maps into a discrete space; sectionwise inverse-limit universal property.

proof.text: Apply Mathlib Module.Finite.exists_comp_eq_id_of_projective to each scalar term. Map the resulting retract equation through the constant and scalar-extension functors. Naturality of the module sheafification unit and the normalized change-of-rings tensor maps give the three section formulas for each splitting map.

source.place: Tags 00NX and 05CF; Mathlib finite projective retract and functoriality.

proof.text: Reuse the fully proved constant_flat and model_good helpers of the existing scalar-model interface, without using its unfinished pullback theorem. Their proof uses the site equational criterion for flatness of constant projective terms, bounded-above flat K-flatness, and preservation of K-flatness and flat terms by change of rings. The additive realization functor maps all zero terms outside the original finite interval to zero.

source.place: Tags 06YQ and 0G7E; constant_flat and model_good proofs in the existing scalar-model interface.

proof.text: For ring-sheaf maps R to B to A, the normalized ordinary scalar-extension adjunctions compose, while restriction of scalars composes canonically. Uniqueness of left adjoints therefore gives a natural isomorphism between the iterated and direct extension functors. Its Hom normalization determines the image of 1 tensor (1 tensor x). Linearity in both scalar actions gives the full formula a tensor (b tensor x) maps to (a pr(b)) tensor x. The coefficient composite equality is the limit projection equation. Whisker with constant realization and map to cochain complexes; functoriality retains the original differentials and gives chain-map naturality.

source.place: Tag 03DA; composition and uniqueness of normalized scalar-extension left adjoints.

proof.text: Specialize the forward formula at b=1 and apply the inverse isomorphism to obtain the inverse formula. Apply the normalized tower unit formula to obtain the quotient augmentation. Expand each successor arrow of quotientTower; the inverse formula, normalized unrestricted transition formula and forward formula give the stipulated quotient transition on every pure tensor.

source.place: Tags 03DA and 05V4; normalized tensor units and quotient transitions.

proof.text: The two normalized adjunction Hom equivalences are injective, so any two reduction maps agreeing on the nested pure tensors are equal. This proves independence of the reductions, without choosing splittings in their construction. For derived naturality, the identity-resolution comparison is the universal derived counit followed by localization of the ordinary reduction isomorphism. Naturality of that counit and chainBalance, and functoriality of localization, prove the specified derived square.

source.place: Tags 06YY and 06YQ; uniqueness of the normalized adjunction maps and naturality of the universal derived counit.
